    Endpoint socles and scalar unit rays #

    For chosen primitive projectives over a split-basic algebra, an endpoint unit acts on a bimodule-socle morphism through its scalar residue. Consequently, two endpoint-unit-equivalent morphisms differ by multiplication by a nonzero scalar as soon as one of them is annihilated by both endpoint Jacobson radicals. This is the linear-algebra bridge used for the deep-contour half of the BGRS semi-normalization argument.

    Prop

    A morphism between chosen primitive projectives lies in the endpoint bimodule socle when both endpoint Jacobson radicals annihilate it.

        In a split-basic distributive category, every endpoint bimodule socle has dimension at most one. This is the formal form of BGRS 1.3 used after Roiter's square-annihilation alternative.

        If one chosen composite of a related nonzero pair of ray paths lies in the endpoint bimodule socle, then the two chosen composites are nonzero scalar multiples.

        For a related pair of nonzero ray paths, vanishing against radical generators at the endpoints is enough to obtain the required nonzero scalar relation between the chosen composites. Ray-path orientation reverses the displayed quiver endpoints, so j supplies the source endomorphism ring and i the target endomorphism ring.
